how: Every file is hand-built in the real record's shape; no byte of a real record is copied. Keys, row kinds and row order follow the spike sessions; every value (session ids, call ids, reasoning ids, paths, encrypted payloads, prompt text, tool descriptions, token counts) is synthetic.

shape_sources.rerun-pack-on: the R-READ-GROK brief s5 pack-on trusted spike session (home2): summary text in both reasoning rows, one agents_md_files entry (project Agents.md), contextWindowTokens 256000, model_id grok-4.7-build, reasoning_effort high
shape_sources.rerun-pack-off: the brief s5 pack-off spike session (home): reasoning rows with an empty summary (encrypted-only), agents_md_files []
shape_sources.rerun-web-fetch: hand-built: no session record holds a web_fetch call (the ACP streams only advertise it); the assistant tool_calls row and the events.jsonl tool_started/tool_completed pair use the read_file call's real shape with the name web_fetch

updates_jsonl: rerun-pack-on/updates.jsonl (W5, C4): hand-built in the shape of the lean run lean-20261013T222527 pack-on cells' updates.jsonl (build 1.0.41): hook_execution updates with event_name, tool_name on tool events, prompt_id on user_prompt_submit, runs[].name and runs[].status.{status, elapsed_ms}, _meta.agentTimestampMs; one tool_call update shows a non-hook row is skipped. Run names follow the real config paths; times and counts are invented. rerun-pack-off has none on purpose (the reader's not-recorded path).
never_copied: the brief s5 never-copy session (its agents_md_files holds the operator's global instruction file, LEAK-HOME-A)
